newsitem.title: USA: NPC Int'l to acquire 122 Pizza Hut units.
newsitem.headline: NPC Int'l to acquire 122 Pizza Hut units.

text.p: NPC International Inc said Friday it had signed a letter of intent with Pizza Hut Inc to acquire 122 Pizza Hut restaurants and associated development areas for $53.5 million.

The restaurants are located in Topeka, Kan.; Beaumont/Port Arthur, Texas; Champaign/Springfield, Ill.; Lake Charles, La.; Evansville, Ind.; Terre Haute, Ind.; Ft. Smith, Ark.; Jackson, Tenn.; Tulsa, Okla.; and Longview, Texas.
The 88 restaurants and 34 delivery carry-out units generated nearly $71 million in sales during the 52 weeks ended November, 1996, NPC said in a statement.

NPC said it is actively pursuing other franchisee locations that are contiguous to the company's territory. After completion of this transaction, NPC will have acquired 176 Pizza Hut units during the last 22 months, for an increase of over 50 percent in the number of Pizza Hut units operated since it's fiscal year ended March 28, 1995.

This acquisition brings NPC's Pizza Hut restaurant holdings to over 530 units. These stores will supplement its presence in the southeastern United States and provide the company with an initial foothold in Illinois, and Indiana.

With this acquisition and continued growth at its Tony Roma restaurants, NPC said it is targeting consolidated revenue in excess of $400 million in fiscal 1998, for an increase of over 30 percent from anticipated fiscal 1997 levels.

To ease the integration of the 122 units, the transaction may be concluded in two separate closings. The company expects the first closing to occur in early March and the second closing, if necessary, to occur in late March or early April.
Completion of the transaction is subject to negotiation of a definitive asset acquisition agreement, board approval of both companies, financing, and approval from regulatory agencies, NPC said.
